records.title: induction using the class equation
records.reason: Lecture 23 proves Sylow I–III by actions on subsets, cosets, and Sylow subgroups; it contains no class-equation induction proof.
records.locator: MIT notes, Lecture 23 §23.3, printed pp. 115–118 (Theorems 23.4, 23.7, 23.8 and proofs).

records.title: polynomial/permutation representation constructions
records.reason: The cited lecture gives the subset/coset conjugation actions only; no separate polynomial or symmetric-group representation construction is proved.
records.locator: MIT notes, Lecture 23 §23.3, printed pp. 115–118.

records.title: principal ideal generator
records.reason: The UIC page introduces projective elimination, Sylvester resultants, and states Bézout in projective space, but does not prove the polynomial ideal principal-generator route.
records.locator: UIC Lecture 2, sections “Projective Coordinates” and “Sylvester resultant method”; Bézout statement in the projective-coordinate discussion.

records.title: alternating binomial expansion
records.reason: The Columbia PDF has the Binomial Inversion section and examples, but the retrieved pages contain no proof of the alternating-sum coefficient cancellation.
records.locator: §4.2 “Binomial Inversion,” printed pp. 25–35; heading and examples, no proof passage.

records.title: Triangulation and edge-face count
records.reason: Lecture 35 states the combinatorial Gauss–Bonnet formula and derives the polygon/edge/vertex count, but does not supply the catalog’s standalone triangulation-invariance proof.
records.locator: MIT 18.950 notes, Lecture 35, Definition 35.3 and Theorem 35.4 (printed pp. 17–18).

records.title: Gauss–Bonnet and curvature
records.reason: Forster gives the geodesic-triangulation proof: angle excess integrates curvature, vertex angles sum to 2π, and 2E=3F yields 2χ; it also states χ=2−2g.
records.locator: Forster, “The Theorem of Gauss-Bonnet in Complex Analysis,” pp. 1–2, theorem and proof following “Euler characteristic.”

records.title: Rectangle/box subdivision and cancellation of interior faces
records.reason: The cited Stokes paper proves the cube case by FTC with opposite face terms canceling, then uses a partition of unity for the general manifold case; this is the stated box-cancellation route in m dimensions.
records.locator: Dresdner, §6, Theorem 6.0.3 proof, pp. 8–9: cube calculation and partition-of-unity reduction.
records.integrationNote: Cube calculation is present, but the general partition-of-unity reduction is asserted without proof.

records.title: differential forms/Stokes
records.reason: Theorem 6.0.3 explicitly proves Stokes on a cube and reduces to compact manifolds by coordinate-supported forms and a partition of unity.
records.locator: Dresdner, §6, Theorem 6.0.3 and proof, pp. 8–9.
records.integrationNote: Cube calculation is present, but the general partition-of-unity reduction is asserted without proof.

records.title: prove with Green's theorem and the Cauchy–Riemann equations
records.reason: The web text gives Cauchy’s integral formula with a proof using the Cauchy–Goursat/Green framework and the punctured contour; the hypotheses and kernel normalization match the route.
records.locator: Complex Analysis, §6.5, Theorem 6.5.1 and hidden Proof 6.5.1; prerequisites §6.3 Cauchy–Goursat.

records.title: triangulation plus angle defect
records.reason: Forster’s proof is exactly the geodesic-triangle angle-excess summation: vertex angle totals and two-triangles-per-edge reduce the integral to 2χ.
records.locator: Forster, pp. 1–2, “Geodesic triangles,” “Euler characteristic,” and proof of Theorem (Gauß–Bonnet).

records.title: index theorem/characteristic classes in generalized forms
records.reason: The cited expository paper contains four proofs of Gauss–Bonnet–Chern and explicitly develops Chern–Weil/characteristic-class and index-theoretic routes; this is broader than the surface sketch but directly supports the generalized route.
records.locator: Xiong, “The Gauss-Bonnet-Chern Theorem on Riemannian Manifolds,” abstract and §§3–6, arXiv:1111.4972 (59-page PDF).

records.title: Polygonal approximation and winding number
records.reason: Lecture 8 proves Jordan using winding number and a tubular-neighborhood local crossing argument, but not the catalog’s polygonal-approximation/annular-limit proof.
records.locator: Colorado notes, Lecture 8 §8.3, “Proof of the Jordan curve theorem,” especially the paragraphs after the winding-number constancy lemma.
records.integrationNote: The source has a different winding-number route; the catalog sketch specifies a polygonal-approximation limit.

records.title: equivalence of finite etale algebras and finite G-sets in a more advanced framing
records.reason: Milne Chapter 8 develops finite étale algebras, finite G-sets, the embedding constructions, and proves the contravariant equivalence theorem under separability assumptions.
records.locator: Milne, Chapter 8, §§8.13–8.22, especially Theorem 8.21 and its proof (printed pp. 109–112).

records.title: Rabinowitsch trick
records.reason: The paper explicitly derives the strong Nullstellensatz from the weak form via Rabinowitsch’s substitution, with the algebraic-closed-field and vanishing hypotheses stated in the introduction and proof discussion.
records.locator: Stevens, “Early Proofs of Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz,” arXiv:2309.14024, introduction and Rabinowitsch discussion (pp. 1–2; see also the cited Rab29 argument).

records.title: Inductively choose a linear combination avoiding finitely many bad coefficients
records.reason: Lecture 12 proves the finite separable primitive element theorem by choosing c outside finitely many roots so α+cβ has distinct conjugate images, then iterating.
records.locator: NPTEL Lecture 12, Theorem 11.3, proof paragraph beginning “We look for a primitive element of the form …”.

records.title: finite-field cyclicity as the finite-field special case
records.reason: The lecture invokes that a finite field’s multiplicative group is cyclic and then proceeds to primitive elements; the cited page does not prove the cyclicity theorem.
records.locator: NPTEL Lecture 12, opening of §11 “The Primitive Element Theorem,” finite-field paragraph before Definition 11.1.

records.title: Eisenstein after substituting x+1 for prime-power cases plus induction/divisibility
records.reason: Conrad proves the x+1 Eisenstein argument for Φ_{p^r} only. The cited §5 does not provide the catalog’s additional induction/divisibility proof for general n in this route.
records.locator: Conrad, §5, Theorem 5.2 and following paragraph, pp. 8–9; prime-power case explicitly identified as an alternate proof.

records.title: Original value-distribution/complex-analysis proof
records.reason: The cited article proves Little Picard via Ahlfors’ geometric lemma; it does not present the catalog’s logarithm-plus-original value-distribution argument.
records.locator: Simonič, arXiv:1506.07019, §§5.1–5.2 (pp. 10–14), Ahlfors lemma and Little Picard proof.

records.title: Nevanlinna theory and logarithmic derivative estimates
records.reason: The article mentions Nevanlinna theory only as later context and does not prove Little Picard using the second main theorem or logarithmic-derivative estimates.
records.locator: Simonič, arXiv:1506.07019, concluding discussion around §7; no Nevanlinna proof of Little Picard.

records.title: differential-geometric/Ahlfors–Schwarz approach
records.reason: The article’s stated purpose and §§5.1–5.2 give the Ahlfors lemma and use hyperbolic metric comparison to prove Little Picard, matching the differential-geometric route.
records.locator: Simonič, arXiv:1506.07019, Theorem 8 and §5.2 “The Little Picard theorem,” pp. 9–14.

records.title: Fourier-slice theorem and Fourier inversion
records.reason: The Münster notes prove the Fourier-slice theorem and use it to establish injectivity of the Radon transform on Schwartz functions; Fourier inversion supplies recovery.
records.locator: Münster notes, Chapter 20, Corollary 191 (Fourier slice theorem), Theorem 202 (Riesz inversion), and the injectivity statement near p. 49.

records.title: filtered back-projection
records.reason: The notes state the Riesz inversion formula and identify the d−1 case as filtered backprojection, with the Fourier-slice derivation and recovery formula.
records.locator: Münster notes, Chapter 20, Theorem 202, Remark 203, and formula following Remark 204 (pp. 47–48).

records.title: moments/polynomial-density arguments
records.reason: The cited chapter proves moment consistency conditions, but does not prove injectivity by polynomial density and compact-support moment annihilation as sketched.
records.locator: Münster notes, Chapter 21, Theorem 208 (Helgason–Ludwig moment conditions); no polynomial-density injectivity proof at the cited chapter locator.
